chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

My nation will not cease to be in goodness as long as they love one another, exchange gifts, fulfill the trust, avoid the forbidden; honor their guests; establish the prayers, and pay the alms-tax. If they do not do so, they will be tested with famine and years (of hardship).
ai.seo_question: What conditions ensure the continued goodness and prosperity of the Muslim community according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith links communal spiritual health to specific social ethics like gift-giving (*tahabbu*) and guest honor (*taqir al-dayf*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on social cohesion as a prerequisite for divine favor. The warning of famine (*qahat*) and years of hardship (*al-sinin*) serves as a tangible consequence of neglecting these duties, a theme often cited in Shia tafsir to explain historical calamities.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-25 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “

Good in my nation will never end for as long as the people are friendly with each other, give each other gifts, return what they are entrusted with, avoid what is forbidden, honor their guests, establish the prayers, and pay the alms-tax. If they do not do so then they will encounter famine and inflation.”
